title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 1. Mercy to Tapana Mishra and Other Dwellers of Kashi on the Way to Vrindavana
html:
The Lord sings and dances at Nilachala with the devotees of Puri and of Gauda, then takes leave of them and, seeing nothing around Him but Vrindavana, hastens northward; at Kashi He stays with Tapana Mishra, blesses his son Raghunatha and turns the people of the city to devotion to Hari

Verse 1

एवं जगौ रासरसान्नीलाचले
श्रीकृष्णसंकीर्तनपूर्णमानसः।
स्वरूपमुख्यैर्गदाधराद्यैः
समं ननर्त स हि नामकौतुकी॥१॥

evaṁ jagau rāsarasānnīlācale
śrīkṛṣṇasaṁkīrtanapūrṇamānasaḥ|
svarūpamukhyairgadādharādyaiḥ
samaṁ nanarta sa hi nāmakautukī||1||

evam — thus; jagau — sang; rasa-rasan — the rasas of the rasa dance; nilachale — at Nilachala; shri-krishna-sankirtana-purna-manasah — His mind filled with the sankirtana of Sri Krishna; svarupa-mukhyaih — headed by Svarupa; gadadhara-adyaih — with Gadadhara and others; samam — together; nanarta — danced; sah — He; hi — indeed; nama-kautuki — delighting in the Name.

1Thus at Nilachala He whose mind was filled with the sankirtana of Sri Krishna sang of the rasas of the rasa dance, and danced together with Svarupa, Gadadhara and the others — He who delights in the Holy Name.

Verse 2

श्रीसार्वभौमेन सह श्रीरामानन्दादयः क्षेत्रनिवासिनो ये।
आजग्मुः श्रीगौररसेन पूर्णाः पपुस्तु हर्षान्मुखपङ्कजं प्रभोः॥२॥

śrīsārvabhaumena saha śrīrāmānandādayaḥ kṣetranivāsino ye|
ājagmuḥ śrīgaurarasena pūrṇāḥ papustu harṣānmukhapaṅkajaṁ prabhoḥ||2||

shri-sarvabhaumena saha — together with Sri Sarvabhauma; shri-ramananda-adayah — Sri Ramananda and the others; kshetra-nivasinah — residents of the Kshetra; ye — who; ajagmuh — came; shri-gaura-rasena — with the rasa of Sri Gaura; purnah — filled; papuh — drank; tu — and; harshat — joyfully; mukha-pankajam — the lotus face; prabhoh — of the Lord.

2Together with Sri Sarvabhauma came Sri Ramananda and the other residents of the Kshetra1, filled with the rasa of Sri Gaura, and joyfully drank in with their eyes the lotus face of the Lord.

Verse 3

शृण्वन्ति संकीर्तननाममङ्गलं
गायन्ति आनन्दसमुद्रमग्नाः।
नृत्यन्ति सर्वे रसिकेन्द्रमौलिना
गौराङ्गचन्द्रेण समं विहस्ताः॥३॥

śṛṇvanti saṁkīrtananāmamaṅgalaṁ
gāyanti ānandasamudramagnāḥ|
nṛtyanti sarve rasikendramaulinā
gaurāṅgacandreṇa samaṁ vihastāḥ||3||

shrinvanti — they hear; sankirtana-nama-mangalam — the auspicious sankirtana of the Name; gayanti — they sing; ananda-samudra-magnah — immersed in an ocean of bliss; nrityanti — they dance; sarve — all; rasika-indra-maulina — with the crown of the kings of rasikas; gauranga-chandrena — with Gaurangachandra; samam — together; vihastah — beside themselves.

3They listen to the auspicious sankirtana of the Name and sing, drowned in an ocean of bliss; and all of them dance, beside themselves, with Gaurangachandra, the crown of the kings of rasikas.

Verse 4

काशीश्वरो राममुकुन्दमुख्यो वक्रेश्वरो राघववासुदेवौ।
श्रीशङ्करश्रीहरिदासगौरीदासादयस्ते हि स गौडवासिनः॥४॥

kāśīśvaro rāmamukundamukhyo vakreśvaro rāghavavāsudevau|
śrīśaṅkaraśrīharidāsagaurīdāsādayaste hi sa gauḍavāsinaḥ||4||

kashishvarah — Kashishvara; rama-mukunda-mukhyah — Rama, Mukunda and the other leading ones; vakreshvarah — Vakreshvara; raghava-vasudevau — Raghava and Vasudeva; shri-shankara-shri-haridasa-gauridasa-adayah — Sri Shankara, Sri Haridasa, Gauridasa and others; te — they; hi — indeed; sa — (expletive); gauda-vasinah — the dwellers of Gauda.

4Kashishvara, Rama, Mukunda and the others foremost among them, Vakreshvara, Raghava and Vasudeva, Sri Shankara, Sri Haridasa, Gauridasa and the rest — the dwellers of Gauda2 —

Verse 5

खण्डस्थिताः श्रीरघुनन्दनादयो
गौराङ्गभावेन विभावितान्तराः।
कुलीनग्रामनिवासिनः सुखं
नृत्यन्ति गायन्ति नमन्ति सन्ततम्॥५॥

khaṇḍasthitāḥ śrīraghunandanādayo
gaurāṅgabhāvena vibhāvitāntarāḥ|
kulīnagrāmanivāsinaḥ sukhaṁ
nṛtyanti gāyanti namanti santatam||5||

khanda-sthitah — those living at Khanda; shri-raghunandana-adayah — Sri Raghunandana and others; gauranga-bhavena — by their feeling for Gauranga; vibhavita-antarah — with hearts imbued; kulina-grama-nivasinah — the dwellers of Kulinagrama; sukham — joyfully; nrityanti — dance; gayanti — sing; namanti — bow down; santatam — unceasingly.

5and Sri Raghunandana and the others who live at Khanda, and the dwellers of Kulinagrama3 — all whose hearts are imbued with feeling for Gauranga — joyfully dance and sing and bow down without cease.

Verse 6

नृत्यावसाने प्रभुरच्युतः स्वयं
प्राह परं भक्तजनानुकम्पवान्।
वृन्दावनं रम्यमतीव दुर्लभं
गच्छामि यच्चेद्भवतां कृपा भवेत्॥६॥

nṛtyāvasāne prabhuracyutaḥ svayaṁ
prāha paraṁ bhaktajanānukampavān|
vṛndāvanaṁ ramyamatīva durlabhaṁ
gacchāmi yaccedbhavatāṁ kṛpā bhavet||6||

nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; prabhuh — the Lord; achyutah — Achyuta; svayam — Himself; praha — said; param — greatly; bhakta-jana-anukampavan — compassionate toward His devotees; vrindavanam — to Vrindavana; ramyam — lovely; ativa — exceedingly; durlabham — hard to attain; gacchami — I shall go; yat chet — if; bhavatam — your; kripa — mercy; bhavet — there be.

6When the dancing was over, the Lord Achyuta Himself, full of compassion for His devotees, said, "If I have your blessing, I shall go to lovely Vrindavana, so very hard to reach."

Verse 7

पिबन्ति गौराङ्गमुखाब्जपीयूषं
पूर्णास्तथा तेऽपि सुदुःखिता भृशम्।
क्रन्दन्ति गौराङ्गपदारविन्दे
निपत्य दन्ताग्रतृणा वदन्ति॥७॥

pibanti gaurāṅgamukhābjapīyūṣaṁ
pūrṇāstathā te'pi suduḥkhitā bhṛśam|
krandanti gaurāṅgapadāravinde
nipatya dantāgratṛṇā vadanti||7||

pibanti — they drink; gauranga-mukha-abja-piyusham — the nectar of Gauranga's lotus face; purnah — filled; tatha — thus; te — they; api — though; suduhkhitah — grieved; bhrisham — deeply; krandanti — weep; gauranga-pada-aravinde — at the lotus feet of Gauranga; nipatya — falling; danta-agra-trinah — with straws between their teeth; vadanti — they say.

7They drink the nectar of Gauranga's lotus face, and though they are filled with it, they are deeply grieved. Weeping, they fall at Gauranga's lotus feet and, with straws between their teeth4, they say:

Verse 8

त्वमेव वृन्दावनचन्द्र हे प्रभो
तथापि दासानुमतेन सर्वम्।
कर्तुं सदा पृच्छसि साम्प्रतं किल
स नन्दनानन्दमुखान्विधेहि नः॥८॥

tvameva vṛndāvanacandra he prabho
tathāpi dāsānumatena sarvam|
kartuṁ sadā pṛcchasi sāmprataṁ kila
sa nandanānandamukhānvidhehi naḥ||8||

tvam — You; eva — indeed; vrindavana-chandra — O Moon of Vrindavana; he prabho — O Lord; tatha api — yet; dasa-anumatena — with Your servants' consent; sarvam — everything; kartum — to do; sada — always; pricchasi — You ask; sampratam — now; kila — then; sah — You; nandana-ananda-mukhan — with faces of joy and bliss; vidhehi — make; nah — us.

8"O Lord, You are the Moon of Vrindavana Himself, and yet You always ask Your servants' consent before You do anything. Then make our faces bright now with joy and bliss!"5

Verse 9

एवं श्रुत्वा हसन् प्राह भवतां सन्निधौ सदा।
तिष्ठामीति ब्रुवन् शीघ्रं गमनाय कृतोद्यमः॥९॥

evaṁ śrutvā hasan prāha bhavatāṁ sannidhau sadā|
tiṣṭhāmīti bruvan śīghraṁ gamanāya kṛtodyamaḥ||9||

evam — thus; shrutva — hearing; hasan — laughing; praha — said; bhavatam — of you; sannidhau — in the presence; sada — always; tishthami — I abide; iti — thus; bruvan — saying; shighram — swiftly; gamanaya — for departure; krita-udyamah — made ready.

9Hearing this, He laughed and said, "I am always with you," and with these words He quickly made ready to depart.

Verse 10

रुदतस्तान् समालिङ्ग्य स सान्त्वय्य पुनः पुनः।
आयास्येति ब्रुवन् कृष्णो ययौ वृन्दावनं शुभम्॥१०॥

rudatastān samāliṅgya sa sāntvayya punaḥ punaḥ|
āyāsyeti bruvan kṛṣṇo yayau vṛndāvanaṁ śubham||10||

rudatah — weeping; tan — them; samalingya — embracing; sah — He; santvayya — consoling; punah punah — again and again; ayasye — I shall come back; iti — thus; bruvan — saying; krishnah — Krishna; yayau — went; vrindavanam — to Vrindavana; shubham — auspicious.

10Embracing them as they wept and consoling them again and again with the words "I shall come back," Krishna set out for auspicious Vrindavana.

Verse 11

सोत्कण्ठं धावतस्तस्य मत्तसिंह इव प्रभोः।
सङ्गिनो बलदेवाद्या धावन्ति तमनुव्रताः॥११॥

sotkaṇṭhaṁ dhāvatastasya mattasiṁha iva prabhoḥ|
saṅgino baladevādyā dhāvanti tamanuvratāḥ||11||

sa-utkantham — with longing; dhavatah — running; tasya — of Him; matta-simhah — a maddened lion; iva — like; prabhoh — of the Lord; sanginah — companions; baladeva-adyah — Baladeva and others; dhavanti — run; tam — after Him; anuvratah — devoted.

11The Lord ran on, full of longing, like a maddened lion, and His companions, Baladeva6 and the others, devotedly ran after Him.

Verse 12

यत्र यत्र पर्वतञ्च नदीश्च परमः प्रभुः।
पश्यन् गोवर्धनं वृन्दावनं कालिन्दीमप्यसौ॥१२॥

yatra yatra parvatañca nadīśca paramaḥ prabhuḥ|
paśyan govardhanaṁ vṛndāvanaṁ kālindīmapyasau||12||

yatra yatra — wherever; parvatam — a hill; cha — and; nadih — rivers; cha — and; paramah — the Supreme; prabhuh — Lord; pashyan — seeing; govardhanam — Govardhana; vrindavanam — Vrindavana; kalindim — the Kalindi; api — also; asau — He.

12Wherever the Supreme Lord saw hills and rivers, He saw in them Govardhana, Vrindavana and the Kalindi7.

Verse 13

मत्तहुङ्कारनिर्घोषो मत्तद्विरदविक्रमः।
नृत्यति धावति रौति क्षितौ विलुठति क्वचित्॥१३॥

mattahuṅkāranirghoṣo mattadviradavikramaḥ|
nṛtyati dhāvati rauti kṣitau viluṭhati kvacit||13||

matta-hunkara-nirghoshah — thundering with intoxicated roars; matta-dvirada-vikramah — striding like a maddened elephant; nrityati — dances; dhavati — runs; rauti — cries out; kshitau — on the ground; viluthati — rolls; kvachit — at times.

13Thundering with intoxicated cries and striding like a maddened elephant, He now dances, now runs, now cries aloud, now rolls on the ground.

Verse 14

एवं क्रमेण भगवान् काशीमुपजगाम ह।
विश्वेश्वरमहालिङ्गदर्शनानन्दविह्वलः॥१४॥

evaṁ krameṇa bhagavān kāśīmupajagāma ha|
viśveśvaramahāliṅgadarśanānandavihvalaḥ||14||

evam — thus; kramena — by stages; bhagavan — the Lord; kashim — to Kashi; upajagama — came; ha — indeed; vishveshvara-maha-linga-darshana-ananda-vihvalah — overwhelmed with bliss at the sight of the great linga of Vishveshvara.

14Going on thus by stages, the Lord came to Kashi, and at the sight of the great linga of Vishveshvara8 He was overwhelmed with bliss.

Verse 15

तत्रैव ब्राह्मणः कश्चित्तपनाख्यः सुवैष्णवः।
पश्यन् प्रभुं महाहृष्टो निनाय निजमन्दिरम्॥१५॥

tatraiva brāhmaṇaḥ kaścittapanākhyaḥ suvaiṣṇavaḥ|
paśyan prabhuṁ mahāhṛṣṭo nināya nijamandiram||15||

tatra eva — right there; brahmanah — a brahmana; kashchit — a certain; tapana-akhyah — named Tapana; su-vaishnavah — a true Vaishnava; pashyan — seeing; prabhum — the Lord; maha-hrishtah — greatly delighted; ninaya — led; nija-mandiram — to his own house.

15There a certain brahmana, a true Vaishnava named Tapana9, saw the Lord, was overjoyed and led Him to his own house.

Verse 16

तेन संपूजितः कृष्णः पादप्रक्षालनादिभिः।
भिक्षां कृत्वा गृहे तस्य सुखासीनो जगद्गुरुः॥१६॥

tena saṁpūjitaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pādaprakṣālanādibhiḥ|
bhikṣāṁ kṛtvā gṛhe tasya sukhāsīno jagadguruḥ||16||

tena — by him; sampujitah — honoured; krishnah — Krishna; pada-prakshalana-adibhih — with the washing of His feet and so on; bhiksham — alms (His meal); kritva — taking; grihe — in the house; tasya — his; sukha-asinah — seated at ease; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world.

16He honoured Krishna by washing His feet and with every other service; and the Teacher of the world, having taken His meal in that house and resting there happily,

Verse 17

तिष्ठति तत्सुतेनापि रघुनाथेन मानितः।
तस्मै महाकृपां चक्रे बालकाय महात्मने॥१७॥

tiṣṭhati tatsutenāpi raghunāthena mānitaḥ|
tasmai mahākṛpāṁ cakre bālakāya mahātmane||17||

tishthati — He stays; tat-sutena — by his son; api — also; raghunathena — by Raghunatha; manitah — honoured; tasmai — to him; maha-kripam — great mercy; chakre — showed; balakaya — to the boy; maha-atmane — great-souled.

17stayed there, honoured also by his son Raghunatha10; and on that great-souled boy He bestowed great mercy.

Verse 18

चन्द्रशेखरवैद्यस्य गृहे तिष्ठन्नपि स्वयम्।
काशीवासिजनान् कुर्वन् हरिभक्तिरतान् किल॥१८॥

candraśekharavaidyasya gṛhe tiṣṭhannapi svayam|
kāśīvāsijanān kurvan haribhaktiratān kila||18||

chandrashekhara-vaidyasya — of Chandrashekhara the vaidya; grihe — in the house; tishthan — staying; api — also; svayam — Himself; kashi-vasi-janan — the people of Kashi; kurvan — making; hari-bhakti-ratan — devoted to bhakti for Hari; kila — indeed.

18And though He Himself lived in the house of Chandrashekhara the physician11, He truly turned the people of Kashi to devotion to Hari:

Verse 19

हरिसंकीर्तनामोदी स्वभक्तगणवेष्टितः।
हरिं वदेति संजल्पन् बाहुमुत्क्षिपति सदा॥१९॥

harisaṁkīrtanāmodī svabhaktagaṇaveṣṭitaḥ|
hariṁ vadeti saṁjalpan bāhumutkṣipati sadā||19||

hari-sankirtana-amodi — delighting in the sankirtana of Hari; sva-bhakta-gana-veshtitah — surrounded by His devotees; harim — "Hari"; vada — say; iti — thus; sanjalpan — calling out; bahum — His arm; utkshipati — throws up; sada — always.

19delighting in the sankirtana of Hari and surrounded by His devotees, He would always throw up His arm and call out, "Say 'Hari'!"

Thus ends the first sarga, "Mercy to Tapana Mishra and Other Dwellers of Kashi on the Way to Sri Vrindavana" (Shri-vrindavana-gamana-purvakam kashi-vasi-tapana-mishra-adi-anugraha), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Kshetra: Purushottama-kshetra, that is, Puri (Nilachala).
  2. Rama here is apparently Nityananda; Raghava is Raghava Pandita, Vasudeva is Vasudeva Datta, and Shankara is Shankara Pandita, the brother of Damodara Pandita.
  3. Khanda (Shrikhanda): the village of Narahari Sarakara and his nephew Raghunandana; Kulinagrama: the village of the Vasu family (Satyaraja Khan and Ramananda Vasu) in Bengal.
  4. A straw between the teeth: a sign of utter humility and supplication.
  5. The reading of the second half of the verse differs between the editions; the translation is conjectural.
  6. Baladeva: the Lord's companion on the journey to Vrindavana, the brahmana Balabhadra Bhattacharya.
  7. The Kalindi: the Yamuna, daughter of Kalinda.
  8. Vishveshvara: the principal linga of Shiva at Kashi (Varanasi).
  9. Tapana Mishra: a brahmana of East Bengal who had received instruction from the Lord during His travels in East Bengal and at His word had settled in Kashi.
  10. Raghunatha: later Raghunatha Bhatta, one of the six Gosvamis of Vrindavana.
  11. Chandrashekhara: a physician (vaidya) and scribe at Kashi, a devotee of the Lord; not to be confused with Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna of Navadvipa.
